question: Does enabling the first textual Python program improve the normalized score at 395 seconds on two previously unused six-period storage cases?

split.unit: An input instance from one synthetic storage-scheduling family. Identical task instructions are intentional.
split.selection: A/B/C informed the original policy; exclude all three from replication statistics. Prepare D/E before any model run. Freeze model, code and scoring before scoring D/E. Once opened, these holdouts cannot confirm later retuning.

arms.legacy: Small-package compact prompt followed by the existing tool loop.
arms.text: Same small-package input and verifier. Enable one first textual Python program with an isolated execution and guard before the normal tool loop.
arms.factor: First Python action module on/off. Its prompt, response interface, first-call limit and feedback change together; no attribution among these pieces.

design.execution: One GitHub-hosted runner per pair. Use separate task containers and model-server processes, reset KV state, repeat the identical function-call warm-up. The downloaded GGUF/binaries may be reused within a pair.
design.interpretation: Repeated executions at one fixed seed and zero temperature measure repeatability across runners; they do not sample decoding seeds or independent task families.

metrics.primary: Independent grade.score at external 395-second cutoff. Score equals reference optimal cost divided by independently recomputed feasible cost. Invalid or absent deliverables score zero.
secondary: first structurally verified action timing when instrumented; not directly comparable across arms
metrics.full_budget_score: Not measured in this experiment. Do not combine with the historical 720-second runs.
metrics.sample_variance: For each repeat, average scores over both cases within each arm, then compute sample mean and sample variance (n-1 denominator) across the three repeat means. Compute paired delta = text minus legacy within each (case, repeat); aggregate the same way. List all six raw pairs and each case's scores.
metrics.missing: A transport/infra failure, unreadable snapshot, unstable cutoff or missing record is unmeasured. Never replace it with a zero; show coverage. Only fully observed case pairs and repeats enter their respective descriptive summaries. No confirmatory decision with any incomplete pair.
metrics.retries: Retain original attempts. Use the first measured result for each arm in the same valid paired execution. Re-run the entire pair only for a technical failure; never select the best score.

decision.positive_same_family: All six pairs measured, neither held-out case has a negative mean paired difference, and all three repeat-level mean differences are positive. Keep the first-action module as a candidate only for small eligible Gemma CPU runs.
decision.otherwise: Mixed, tied or incomplete evidence does not support a general default switch. Keep both strategies available for controlled experiments.
decision.official: Never promote the official competition configuration on the strength of these two same-family cases. Confirm on a separately frozen task family or official evaluation.

reproducibility.authoritative_experiment_code: Use the exact Actions run head SHA for the workflow, generator, grader and all runtime source. The scorer runs on the host; only task.md and the two input files enter the task container.
reproducibility.release: Present measured conclusions, per-arm and paired uncertainty, case-level results and a plot before composing the submission narrative. Publish failures and coverage alongside successful cases.
